about: Known-answer vectors for CanonicalPayloadHasher, specified in the Known-answer vectors section
of docs/event-contract.md. Each entry pairs a wire event with the hashes this repository has
Comparing two hashes computed in the same process proves nothing about determinism: both move
together when the serializer, the runtime or the canonical model changes. These constants were
computed by an earlier build in a different process and do not move, which is what makes them a
cross-process and cross-version check rather than a self-consistency one.
A vector failing after an SDK or runtime upgrade is the intended signal. It means canonicalisation
changed, and every idempotency record written before the upgrade now hashes differently, so
replays would be reclassified as conflicts. Treat it as a schema migration, never as a test to

vectors.name: reference
vectors.why: The reference event from docs/event-contract.md, with a null causationId as a root event has.

vectors.name: caused-event
vectors.why: The reference event with a causationId present. Pins that the field is inside the envelope scope, so a root event and a caused one are not duplicates of each other.

vectors.name: unknown-top-level-fields
vectors.why: The reference event carrying fields this schema version does not know about, in a different property order. Its hashes are the reference vector's, which is the committed form of the forward-compatibility rule.

vectors.name: same-data-new-event-id
vectors.why: A legitimate republish of the reference order: new eventId, later occurredAtUtc, new correlationId, identical data. Shares the reference vector's business hash and differs in its envelope hash, which is the whole reason two hashes exist.

vectors.name: non-ascii-item-description
vectors.why: Pins string escaping, which the serializer options cannot state. A change to how a non-ASCII character or a quotable one is written changes these bytes and nothing else would notice.

vectors.name: extreme-amount
vectors.why: The largest representable minor-unit amount, and single-character identifiers. Pins integer rendering at the boundary where a formatting change or a narrower numeric type would show.
